name: Higashi-Ginza
tagline: Toranomon in 6 minutes and Tokyo in 9 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥160,000 to ¥170,000.
summary: The station is in Chuo City, where Tokyo Metro and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 10 minutes to Otemachi, 22 minutes to Shinjuku, 22 minutes to Shibuya and 14 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. The station stands 2.9 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 1.9 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 2.9 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 2.1 m to 4 m, a difference of 1.9 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 7 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 3 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is about average for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 13 clinics and 8 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 国立がん研究センター中央病院, about 8 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 十仁病院, about 13 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line run through it. Toei Asakusa Line also call here. The lines are split between operators (Tokyo Metro runs 1 line and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line runs at 163% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 三ノ輪→入谷, which this station is not on. Toei Asakusa Line runs at 123%. Its busiest stretch is 本所吾妻橋→浅草, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥160,000 to ¥170,000 and 1K ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. 1LDK ¥240,000 to ¥250,000 and 2LDK ¥330,000 to ¥340,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. plenty of places to eat out pushes the figure up. On the other side, little daily shopping within walking distance and many bars by the station and voices outside late at night holds it down. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Ginza; for lower rent, Higashi-Ginza.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Higashi-Ginza. Ginza also has the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line and Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line, which Higashi-Ginza does not. With more lines, Ginza is the better connected of the two. To Tokyo, for instance, Ginza is 6 minutes quicker. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥10,000 more at Ginza.

neighbours.lead: For lower rent, Tsukijishijo; for rail connections, Higashi-Ginza.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Higashi-Ginza. Tsukijishijo has only the Toei Oedo Line, so Higashi-Ginza is the better connected. To Otemachi, for instance, Tsukijishijo takes 11 minutes longer. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥14,000 less at Tsukijishijo.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
People who want to hold the rent down
noiseSources: The 首都高速都心環状線 viaduct runs just outside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
晴海通り (3 lanes each way) runs right beside the station. Traffic on it never stops, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 1 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 9 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are some of the most heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
